BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

Of course. As your legal advisor, I have reviewed the Seller's updated draft positions and Disclosure Letter against the Wattlebridge Holdings negotiation playbook for Project Kestrel.

The Seller's proposal represents a significant departure from our baseline in almost every critical area. Their strategy is clear: to shift risk to the Buyer by lowering liability caps, raising claim thresholds, narrowing disclosure, and weakening specific protections for known issues.

Here is a detailed analysis of the departures and our recommended pushback.

---

### **1. General Warranty Liability Cap (Clause 12.1)**

*   **Seller's Position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
*   **Playbook Departure:** This matches our conditional fallback position. However, the playbook is explicit: this cap is **only** usable with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the specific draft. No such authority has been given.
*   **Our Pushback:** We must reject this outright. Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. We should state that we are not in a position to accept the 20% cap without Amelia Frost's specific approval. We should reiterate our 25% position as the agreed baseline.

### **2. Claim Thresholds (Clause 12.2)**

*   **Seller's Position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; Basket of AUD 250,000, with recovery only for the **excess** above the basket.
*   **Playbook Departure:** This is a major departure. Our playbook sets a much lower de minimis (AUD 5,000) and, crucially, a **"seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded"** aggregate basket of AUD 50,000. The Seller's proposal makes it much harder to claim for smaller issues and excludes the first AUD 250,000 of claims entirely.
*   **Our Pushback:** Strong rejection. We must insist on our thresholds: AUD 5,000 de minimis and an AUD 50,000 basket where the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the aggregate is exceeded.

### **3. Time Limits & Fundamental Warranties (Clauses 12.3 / 13)**

*   **Seller's Position:** General claims period of 18 months. Proposes that **all claims** (including fundamental/title) be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
*   **Playbook Departure:** This is a critical attack on our protection.
    *   The 18-month general claims period is a fallback requiring Amelia's written approval (not given).
    *   More seriously, the Seller seeks to collapse the separate, stronger regime for Fundamental/Title claims (100% cap, at least six years, outside baskets/de minimis) into the weak general warranty regime.
*   **Our Pushback:**
    *   **General Claims Period:** Reject 18 months. Insist on 24 months.
    *   **Fundamental/Title Claims:** **Absolute red line.** We must firmly reject any attempt to apply the general warranty cap and time limit to title, capacity, or fundamental warranties. These must remain on a separate, superior footing as per our playbook.

### **4. Limitations & Reliance (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)**

*   **Seller's Position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**.
*   **Playbook Departure:** This directly undermines our playbook's mandate for a **carve-out for Fraud, Wilful Concealment, and Deliberate Misconduct** from all caps, baskets, time limits, and exclusive remedies. This is our most important protection.
*   **Our Pushback:** **Non-negotiable.** We must insert an explicit carve-out stating that the limitations in Clauses 12 and 20 do not apply to any claim arising from fraud, wilful concealment, or deliberate misconduct by the Seller. This must be to the maximum extent enforceable at law.

### **5. Disclosure (Schedule 7 & Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2])**

*   **Seller's Position:** Relies on "general disclosure of the data room and public registers."
*   **Playbook Departure:** This is exactly the "whole-data-room" and "public-register" deemed disclosure we are instructed to reject.
*   **Our Pushback:** Reject the concept of general disclosure. We must require **specific, fair disclosure** of all known material matters. The Disclosure Letter must list specific risks and circumstances, not just point to a data room. We should demand the removal of any language that deems the data room contents as sufficient disclosure for warranty breaches.

### **6. Buyer Knowledge (Clause 8.3)**

*   **Seller's Position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers **had knowledge**, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
*   **Playbook Departure:** This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion we are to delete. It improperly excuses the Seller from liability for matters we should have no claim on (like title or capacity) and uses an overly broad "discoverable" standard.
*   **Our Pushback:** Delete this clause entirely. If the Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier, it must be strictly limited to **named seller knowledge persons** and require the Buyer to have failed to conduct a **reasonable enquiry**. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnities.

### **7. Bluefen Consent (Clause 3 / 6.3 & Disclosure Letter [2])**

*   **Seller's Position:** "Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
*   **Playbook Departure:** The playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**. "Reasonable endeavours" is explicitly deemed insufficient for a material customer consent. The Seller has not provided the final consent or evidence of condition satisfaction.
*   **Our Pushback:** This is a major risk. We must change the condition to require the Seller to **obtain and provide to the Buyer, prior to Completion, the final, effective Bluefen consent and evidence that all its pre-conditions are satisfied.** This is a condition precedent to our obligation to complete.

### **8. Riverlark Bank Facility (Clause 2 / 7 & Disclosure Letter [3])**

*   **Seller's Position:** Facility (~AUD 3.2M) to be addressed by a release **following Completion**.
*   **Playbook Departure:** The playbook requires a **current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases**. A post-completion release is unacceptable without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval, neither of which is present.
*   **Our Pushback:** **Reject post-completion release.** We must require that the Riverlark facility is repaid in full from the Completion funds, and that the bank provides irrevocable, signed releases of all security **before** we release the funds to the Seller.

### **9. Employee Bonuses (Funds Flow & Disclosure Letter [5])**

*   **Seller's Position:** Bonuses (AUD 420k) are a "matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. No mention of on-costs.
*   **Playbook Departure:** The playbook requires these to be a **specific line item or seller-funded** and that the funds flow must not silently exclude them and their on-costs.
*   **Our Pushback:** Demand that the AUD 420,000 and all associated triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) be explicitly accounted for as a deduction from the purchase price in the Completion funds flow, ensuring they are paid in full upon Completion.

### **10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 & Disclosure Letter [4])**

*   **Seller's Position:** Indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."
*   **Playbook Departure:** The playbook requires us to **broaden the narrow indemnity** and preserve the SOW3 cure right. The Seller is trying to close down this protection.
*   **Our Pushback:** Insist on broadening the indemnity to cover any claims related to the Ironquay IP beyond just the SOW3 payment. We must also preserve our right to "cure" the underlying issue (e.g., non-payment) if the Seller fails to do so.

### **11. Export/Privacy Incident (Disclosure Letter [6])**

*   **Seller's Position:** Describes it as a "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material.
*   **Playbook Departure:** The playbook instructs us to **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty, or numeric demand**. The Seller's characterization is premature and seeks to minimize the issue.
*   **Our Pushback:** Reject the characterization. We must require the Seller to **preserve all logs, conduct a full investigation, and provide us with regular updates**. The SPA must contain specific warranties regarding the investigation and remediation, without any materiality threshold.

### **12. Title (Disclosure Letter [10])**

*   **Seller's Position:** Points to the Company share register at DD-012 as evidence of title.
*   **Playbook Departure:** The playbook states the DD-012 register is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof**.
*   **Our Pushback:** We must require the Seller to provide **independent evidence of title**, such as a recent title report or confirmation from the share registry, not just the internal register.

---

### **Summary of Recommendations**

1.  **Reject the Entire Package as a Starting Point:** The Seller's update is not a good-faith negotiation but a series of aggressive positions that undermine our core protections.
2.  **Prioritise Red Lines:** The most critical issues to hold firm on are:
    *   **Fraud/Wilful Concealment Carve-Out:** Non-negotiable.
    *   **Separate Fundamental/Title Warranty Regime:** Non-negotiable.
    *   **Effective Bluefen Consent as a Condition Precedent:** Must be obtained before Completion.
    *   **Pre-Completion Repayment of Riverlark Facility:** Reject any post-completion release.
3.  **Revert to Playbook Baselines:** For all general terms (cap, thresholds, claims period, disclosure, knowledge), we must revert to our stated baseline positions (25% cap, 24-month period, specific disclosure, etc.).
4.  **Demand Specifics on Known Issues:** The funds flow must account for bonuses, the Ironquay indemnity must be broadened, and the export incident must be treated as an open investigation requiring specific warranties.
5.  **Escalate to Amelia Frost:** The 20% cap and 18-month claims period are conditional fallbacks. We must formally notify Amelia Frost of the Seller's proposal and seek her written authority to use these fallbacks, or instruct her that we are holding the line at our baseline positions.

The Seller's document requires a comprehensive mark-up that re-establishes our playbook's protective framework. I am ready to draft the response and the revised SPA clauses.
